newsitem.title: USA: Florida lawmakers ban late term abortion.
newsitem.headline: Florida lawmakers ban late term abortion.

text.p: A bill prohibiting a late-term abortion procedure was on its way to the Florida governor's desk after state senators voted Thursday to ban the technique that has been the focus of national debate.

By a 28-9 vote, the senators banned a procedure known as "dilation and extraction" in which the foetus is partially delivered and an instrument is used to destroy the brain. It has come under fire from groups who call it barbaric.
Florida's senate followed the lead of the House, which voted this week to prohibit physicians from performing the procedure, called "partial birth abortion" by opponents.
"How anyone can justify this is abhorent," said Sen. John Ostalkiewicz, an Orlando Republican. "This is not about pro-life or pro-choice, this is about killing a baby."

Opponents of the ban, who unsuccessfully tried to amend the measure to allow for the procedure when the life or health of the mother was in danger, say the issue is a medical decision that should be left to a woman and her physician.

"We as legislators from our ivory tower in Tallahassee are telling women around the state of Florida what to do and how to do it without medical advice or consultation," said Sen. Ron Klein, a Boca Raton Democrat. "This is a medical procedure."

Since President Clinton vetoed a federal measure outlawing the procedure in April 1996, at least six states have voted to ban it, an analysis compiled by the Florida Senate said. Variations have been introduced in at least 30 states.

Critics of the Florida bill, a coalition of groups including Planned Parenthood and the American Civil Liberties Union, have vowed to challenge it in court if it is not vetoed by Gov. Lawton Chiles. Chiles has said he has yet to make up his mind on the issue.
